Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (Cobalt - Head of Security), Diego Marquez (Cobalt - Platform), Priya Singh (Cobalt - IAM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete):
- Walkthrough of SAML + SCIM onboarding and RBAC role matrix for Cobalt's multi-tenant control plane.
- Discussed least-privilege patterns, audit/log retention, encryption/KMS, and Private/VPC deployment considerations.
- Agreed next steps: share certs and sample metadata; SE to demo SCIM provisioning; customer to validate role definitions.

Topics covered:

- SCIM provisioning cadence and attribute mapping

- Encryption at rest (KMS/HSM) and in transit

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um, we're gonna focus on the access guardrails piece and SSO ops readiness - quick round intros?
[00:08] Anika Rao: Hi, Anika here - head of security at Cobalt. We're evaluating SSO + automated provisioning because our current onboarding is manual and slow.
[00:15] Diego Marquez: Diego, platform, we'll own the infra bits.
[00:17] Priya Singh: Priya - IAM admin, I'll be doing the IdP side.
[00:20] Maya Chen: Great. Liam from engineering will take us through the SAML/SCIM flows and recommended RBAC pattern. Liam?
[00:27] Liam O'Connor: Thanks. So high level - Redwood supports SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML, metadata import, cert rollover, and SCIM v2 for provisioning. The common pattern we see is map IdP groups to Redwood roles, keep role definitions small and use attribute-based rules for exceptions.
[00:45] Priya Singh: Quick question, do you support group-to-role sync or should we sync users and then map via attributes?
[00:52] Liam O'Connor: We support both. For larger orgs group-to-role is easier, but it's important to restrict SCIM patch permissions to only manage memberships, not admin flags.
[01:05] Anika Rao: Security perspective: we want least privlege. We can't have broad roles that get admin by default, and we need audit trails for who promoted roles. Are the audit logs tamper-evident?
[01:18] Liam O'Connor: Logs are immutable in the Console append-only index, with integrity checks. For Private customers we can also stream logs to customer-owned S3 or an SIEM via Kinesis. There is a slight nuance on retention tiers - platform stores 90 days by default, extended retention is an add-on.
[01:38] Diego Marquez: What about data residency? Our teams in EU need logs kept in eu-west-1.
[01:44] Maya Chen: We have region-level routing and can pin audit storage to region for Private or Dedicated setups. Hosted customers can request region residency for logs and tensor artifacts but there are compliance review steps.
[01:58] Priya Singh: SCIM cadence - if we have daily syncs, is there support for incremental changes only? We don't want to re-provision every run.
[02:07] Liam O'Connor: SCIM v2 supports incremental patch operations. Our SCIM connector uses delta syncs by default; full syncs are only on demand. Also we rate-limit provisioning calls to protect the runtime.
[02:22] Anika Rao: KMS - we use AWS KMS with external access controls and key rotation policies. Can you integrate with our CMKs?
[02:29] Liam O'Connor: Yes, for Private deployment we support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key). For Hosted, we offer encryption keys managed by Redwood with HSM backing, and we also have a KMS integration for enterprise customers that allows you to hold CMKs in your account and we use a key broker for envelope encryption.
[02:44] Maya Chen: Quick clarification on RBAC: are you recommending role-per-service or role-per-team?
[02:50] Liam O'Connor: We usually advise a hybrid. Role-per-team for day-to-day access, and role-per-service for highly-privileged actions (like model rollout or billing). Keep the admin privileges in separate service roles, and use canaries/canary deploys for rollout approvals.
[03:06] Priya Singh: How do we handle just-in-time elevated access for SREs needing temporary admin to debug incidents?
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: We integrate with SSO sessions/SCIM to grant temporary memberships and we support TTL on role bindings. You can require MFA re-auth and an approval workflow.
[03:22] Anika Rao: Okay, can you show the sample role matrix you mentioned?
[03:25] Liam O'Connor: Sure I'll share the CSV after the call but quick live snapshot: 
- Viewer: read-only on routes, no model management
- Developer: can create routes and call models but cannot change billing or rollout policies
- Operator: can manage autoscale and pools but not billing
- Admin: full privileges (kept minimal)
[03:50] Maya Chen: We'll also include a recommended mapping from IdP group names to those roles, with exceptions for service accounts.
[03:58] Diego Marquez: Regarding service accounts, do you support key-based service principals for machine-to-machine calls? We prefer not to use human SSO for long-running jobs.
[04:06] Liam O'Connor: Yes, Redwood supports API keys scoped to routes and service principals with limited permissions, and those can be rotated automatically. We also support short-lived tokens issued by the Console for ephemeral jobs.
[04:20] Priya Singh: On the SCIM attributes - we use manager and department attributes to infer approvers, but our IdP sometimes normalizes department names differently. How strict are matching rules?
[04:31] Liam O'Connor: Matching can be configured to use regex or normalized mappings. We recommend a canonical mapping table in SCIM transformations. We'll include an example mapping file in the follow-up.
[04:43] Anika Rao: SOC2 and ISO - do you provide the full report or an attestation? Also, does Redwood's Private deploy get included in your SOC scope?
[04:53] Maya Chen: We can share SOC 2 Type II reports and ISO27001 certificate; the Private deployments are typically covered under our enterprise package and can be included in the scope per contract terms. We'll include the auditor contact if you need a direct Q/A.
[05:07] Diego Marquez: Network talk - VPC peering vs private-link - what do you recommend for minimal egress?
[05:13] Liam O'Connor: For lowest egress and dedicated control plane, VPC peering or private link to our dedicated endpoints works. For air-gapped requirements we provide an on-prem package but that'll need more ops coordination.
[05:27] Priya Singh: Are there encryption-in-transit cert requirements? Our security policy mandates mTLS between services.
[05:33] Liam O'Connor: Redwood supports TLS1.2+ and can be configured for mutual TLS for Private/Dedicated. For Hosted we support TLS with client cert options for certain endpoints; we'll capture exact cert requirements in the follow-up doc.
[05:46] Anika Rao: Auditability - if a user escalates privileges, what's the trail? We need to show who approved and who triggered the change.
[05:55] Liam O'Connor: Every role change is logged with actor ID, source (UI/API/SCIM), timestamp, and an optional justification field. For elevated temporary grants we require an approval artifact that is stored in the audit log. Those logs are queryable and can be exported to SIEM.
[06:13] Maya Chen: Let's cover some edgecases - how do you handle model artifacts or KV cache access? We don't want service accounts to exfil model weights or cached prompts.
[06:24] Liam O'Connor: Access to model artifacts is separated from inference call permissions; only certain service roles can download artifacts. KV cache is ephemeral and stored encrypted; access is through runtime APIs and controlled by route-level ACLs. We'll document the exact APIs and controls in the security pack.
[06:42] Diego Marquez: For our compliance team, retention policies are strict - can we set per-tenant retention windows for logs?
[06:49] Liam O'Connor: Yes for Dedicated/Private you can set per-tenant retention. Hosted has preset tiers but enterprise customers can request custom retention with an add-on.
[06:59] Priya Singh: Anything else on SCIM? How about deprovisioning timelines for offboarding?
[07:04] Liam O'Connor: SCIM can be configured to immediate deprovision on disable, or to mark disabled then run cleanup job. We recommend immediate for security-sensitive teams.
[07:15] Anika Rao: Let's jot down the acceptance criteria for our pilot: 1) IdP metadata imported and validated, 2) SCIM provisioning test with 100 users and attribute mapping, 3) audit logs exported to our S3 bucket, 4) role matrix validated and TTL for elevated roles enforced.
[07:35] Maya Chen: Sounds good. I'll capture those as next steps and action items. Liam will send the SCIM demo and example files.
[07:42] Diego Marquez: Timeline wise we want to pilot in staging next week if possible.
[07:46] Maya Chen: We'll aim for week of 2026-10-25.
[07:49] Priya Singh: Perfect. Anything else?
[07:51] Anika Rao: One last quick Q - do you support SCIM transactional batches or do you expect eventual consistency?
[07:58] Liam O'Connor: SCIM is eventually consistent; we do offer transactional hooks for critical ops but generally we design for eventual consistency. We'll flag potential race conditions in our guide.
[08:10] Maya Chen: Okay great, I'll follow up with the security pack and the auditor contact. Thanks everyone.
[08:16] Diego Marquez: Thanks.
[08:17] Priya Singh: Thank you.
[08:18] Anika Rao: Appreciate it.

Call ended.
